title.narrative: Loan 2649: 100% of contracts awarded and 100% disbursed as of 17 Jun 2022

Progress Toward Outcome: The Micro Financing Institute, BRAC was engaged to form and validate small farmers' groups (SFG) and to extend credit support for the interested farmers. Targeted farmer's group formation on-going through validation and new selection. DAE in close collaboration with BRAC arranged technical training for the selected farmers on high value crops production and value addition, and making them eligible for credit support. As of 30 December 2016, total 12,000 SFGs (5,620 male group) enrolling total 263,085 members (142,131 female). Agriculture Credit was availed by 205,229 member farmers (123,425 female) amounting Tk 7,051.7 million (Tk 4,485.9 million to female). BRAC has deployed qualified field staff for group mobilization, awareness raising, helping to arrange technical training and extending credit support. DAE field staff in collaboration with the BRAC) organized field demonstration trials in the potential farmers field for the selected small farmers groups to show potential production technologies. PMU is organizing capacity development training for field staff to better serve the farmers organized under small farmers group. Community facilitators have been recruited and deployed in the field. The project is now in the process of financial closing as the government has to refund the unused fund to ADB. The physical work has been closed on 31 December 2016.
Some results are in the Social Monitoring Reports | Dec 2016: https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/project-documents/40534/40534-013-smr-en.pdf

Status of Implementation Progress: To increase the HVC production and its commercialization, technical training on HVCs production provided to 304,675 farmers and Credit disbursed to 205,229 farmers amounting Tk 7,051.7 million. For HVC demonstration plots, total 17,071 demonstration trials organized in the farmer's field to disseminate HVCs modern production technologies and 1,817 farmers field days organized at demonstration sites. Field activities are ongoing. The NGO (BRAC) engaged and qualified field staff deployed. Agreement between BRAC and wholesale banks (Eastern Bank Ltd. and BASIC Bank Ltd) were signed. Bangladesh Bank as the EA of Credit component is monitoring the credit facilities. Credit fund were channeled through wholesale banks to BRAC to extend credit support to the beneficiaries. Project proceeded towards increased HVC production. As of 30 December 2016, about 84,433 ha of land were converted for HVC production. Actions regarding adaptation to the negative effects of climate change targeted through at least five replicable pilot projects established in the drought-prone areas of the northwest, and five in the southwest areas vulnerable to cyclones and salinity have been completed. To reduce the Postharvest losses, 103 farmer marketing association were formed and 365 ToT completed. For enhancement of market efficiency, total 104 sites selected for establishing On Firm Small Scale Infrastructure (OFSSI). Among them 92 OFSSIs have been completed and are operational through Farmers Marketing Associations (FMA). To enhance the capacity of public sector institutions, 75 staff were provided wtih TOT training on gender, 1,564 DAE and MFI staff received gender awareness training in HVCs and value addition. Experts have also been mobilized for feasibility study on farmer quality, standards, and certification system for fruit and vegetables and a report has been submitted to DAE with recommendations. To increase participation of women in commercial agricultural activities, technical training on HVCs production were provided to 168,550 of female farmers, 1,564 DAE and MFI staff received gender awareness training in HVCs and value addition. Also a plan has been developed to provide group leader (25) training in each Upazila using Gender consultant to create women leaders. Training has been given on climate change adaptability to 13,075 farmers of which 54% are female. Wives and husbands had jointly signed the loan agreements for credit facility programs which gave generated empowerment. Till now, 65% of female credit recipients actively manage the credit.
